content:
According to the Financial Times, new court documents show that OpenAI is disappointed with the adoption of ChatGPT via Apple Intelligence, stating that its performance has "fallen far short of expectations" since its launch in 2024. Details are as follows.

OpenAI is asking the court to issue a ruling before the trial

In August 2025, Elon Musk said that X, now under SpaceXAI, would sue Apple and OpenAI over allegations of conspiring to shut out competitors in the AI space. This stems from OpenAI's deal with Apple to make ChatGPT part of Apple Intelligence and Siri.

When the lawsuit was filed, its scope actually went beyond Musk's original public complaint about App Store rankings. X and SpaceXAI also accused Apple of trying to stifle the development of "super apps," including X's efforts to turn itself into an "everything app."

Over the following weeks and months, all the companies involved filed submissions, allegations and defences with the court. Both Apple and OpenAI raised multiple arguments, including that their deal was not the exclusive partnership the lawsuit claimed; and the court filings also revealed new details about how the partnership operates behind the scenes.

One of those details was exposed in a filing OpenAI made today. The Financial Times first reported that OpenAI "said it was disappointed by how little interest iPhone users had shown after striking the 2024 deal with Apple to power 'Apple Intelligence' with ChatGPT."

The report reads as follows:

Wednesday's court filing noted that when the 2024 deal was struck, OpenAI expected to gain a "halo effect" from the promotional and brand association with Apple, along with more subscriptions from Apple Intelligence users. But one month after the ChatGPT integration launched, it "appeared to get off to a slow start," and OpenAI began lowering its forecasts for weekly active users. By summer 2025, "it had become clear that Apple's ChatGPT integration had performed far below expectations," the filing said.

Today's filing contains several redacted passages, but unredacted portions show that OpenAI executives feared Apple might "want to move faster" and find another AI partner, the report said.

When Apple Intelligence was first unveiled in 2024, Craig Federighi said in an interview that Apple ultimately wanted users to be able to choose between different AI models, specifically mentioning that Google Gemini could be a future integration option.

That particular partnership never came to fruition, but Apple subsequently turned to Google's Gemini model to power the new Siri AI features, while Xcode has also been expanded to support coding agent tools from Anthropic, Google and OpenAI.

Top comment from OliveCocktail

As others have said, when I want to use ChatGPT, I go directly to its standalone app. In fact, that's my preference, because I don't want all my voice requests mixed together. I prefer Apple handling my personalisation and context-aware stuff. I've never been clear on the privacy implications of using the ChatGPT "integration," and I don't even want to find out, because I know I won't use it. By contrast, I feel much more at ease about the privacy side of using Apple Intelligence / Siri.

Returning to today's filing, the Financial Times noted that the documents also raised the way Apple implemented ChatGPT as potentially one reason for the slow adoption, since the integration is off by default.

Finally, according to Reuters, OpenAI has also argued in the dispute that SpaceX's recent securities filings have undermined SpaceXAI's allegations that the Apple deal harms competition. In its filing, OpenAI said SpaceX's IPO registration statement is full of disclosures that are "directly contrary to the competitive harms alleged in the lawsuit."

On these grounds, OpenAI is asking Judge Mark Pittman to rule in its favour on SpaceXAI's antitrust claims before trial. The case is currently scheduled to go to trial in January.
